column2: One beginning with Siddha and ending with Siddha succeeds at that very moment; one beginning with Susiddha and ending in Susiddha one should arrange like Siddha.
An "Ari" at the beginning and likewise at the end one should avoid from afar. Siddha and Susiddha are of one meaning; Ari and Sadhya likewise.
If Siddha stands at the beginning of the mantra, and likewise at its end, then thousands of enemies in the middle do not become a fault.
With the Maya, Prasada and Pranava seeds there is the "part" in the famed mantra: a Brahma-part is Brahma-knowledge, a Vishnu-limb is remembered as Vaishnava;
a Rudra-part would be heroic; an Indra-part dear to the Lord; a Naga-part has a serpent's stiff gaze; a Yaksha-part loves ornament;
a Gandharva-part is much given to song; a Bhima-part a Rakshasa-part; a Daitya-part is for battle-work; a Vidyadhara-part is proud;
a Pishacha-part is covered with impurity; one should give the mantra after examining. A mantra from one up to "phat"; the knowledge up to fifty;
Bala up to twenty syllables; Rudra up to twenty-two with weapons; the mantras above that increase up to three hundred.
From "a" to "ha" in order are the two fortnights, bright and dark; without anusvara and visarga the vowels are ten;
short ones white, long ones dark; the tithis beginning with pratipad. In the "risen" are peace-rites and the like; in the "whirled," subjugation and the like;
in the "whirled," junctures, hatred, banishing, stopping, and setting. Here in invocation peace and the like; in the tawny, attracting and the like;
killing, banishing and the like at the equinox, fivefold separately. In the house below, earth; above, fire; between, liquid;

at the cavity side, outer wind, Maheshvara pervading all. Stopping in the earth-element; peace in water; subjugation and the like in fire; whirling in wind; in space one should practice the time of merit.
Lalita, Subhaga, Gauri, Kshobhani, and from fire in order Vama, Jyeshtha, Kriya, Jnana — one should worship in the circle from the east.
On the seat, at the left side of Shiva, the unmanifest form; the manifest two-eyed, three-syllabled, pure, or with Shankara.
A pair of seat-lotuses, Tara, two- or four-armed, on a lion or wolf, with eight or eighteen good hands,
with garland, rosary, bud, a throat-lotus ball, bearing in the right hand an arrow or bow, either;
in the left a book, betel, staff, fearlessness, water-pot. One should give Ganesha, mirror and bow one by one in order.
Manifest or unmanifest should be made; the lotus mudra is remembered for the seat; the linga mudra is told for Shiva; the invoking mudra for both;
the Shakti mudra is called Yoni; the mandala is four-cornered; a four-cornered three-petalled lotus in the four middle compartments;
in the triangle's upper part a half-moon, a two-square, doubling in order; double the door-neck; double from the near-neck;
three doors, three in the directions; or one should worship in a Bhadra; or having established on a platform with the five cow-products, nectar and the rest,
red flowers should be given; having worshipped facing north; having offered a hundred of nectar-ghee and a full oblation, he is a sharer of all success.
Having given the offering, one should feed three or eight maidens; the food offering should be given to devotees of Shiva, not eaten oneself.
One seeking a maiden gets a maiden; the sonless gets a son; the unfortunate woman good fortune; a king kingdom and victory in battle;
by eight lakh, speech-success; gods and others come under control. One should not eat without offering, and not worship with the left hand;
on the eighth, fourteenth and especially the third. I shall tell the Mrityunjaya worship: one should worship in the belly of a pot.
In the one being offered, Pranava, the form is Ojas thus; with the root mantra ending in "vaushat" one should show the pot mudra;
one should offer milk, durva, ghee, amrita and punarnava, pudding and pindas; one should recite the mantra ten thousand times:
four-faced, four-armed, holding a pot in two arms, with boon and fearlessness in two, one should bathe with the pot mudra;
health, lordship, long life: the consecrated medicine is auspicious. Meditated on, he removes untimely death; worshipped, he is wonderful indeed.
Houses, temples, lingas and the like should be purified thus. "Skanda, homage to Shiva" — the mantra accomplishing all aims.
The five-syllabled is sung in the Veda; in the world the six-syllabled is sung. Shambhu stands at the end as "Om"; for the mudra's sake like a banyan seed.
In order "namah Shivaya" — they know Ishana and the rest. A commentary-collection of knowledge on the sutra of six syllables:
Om namah Shivaya — this much is the supreme station. With this one should worship the linga, since Shiva abides in the linga,
for the favor of the worlds, giving dharma, desire, wealth and liberation. One who does not worship the linga is not a vessel of dharma and the rest.
From worship of the linga, enjoyment and liberation; therefore one should worship as long as life lasts. Better to abandon life than to eat without worshipping him.
By worship of Rudra one becomes Rudra; by worship of Vishnu, Vishnu; by worship of the Sun, the Sun; by worship of Shakti, Shakti and the rest.
Whatever fruit in all sacrifices, austerities, gifts, holy places and Vedas, that fruit a man obtains crore-fold by installing a linga.
One who at the three twilights worships a linga made of earth with bilva — up to eleven hundred, having lifted the family, shares heaven.
One should make a store of grace with devotion according to wealth; in small or great the fruit is equal for rich and poor.
One should arrange two parts for dharma and wealth and for livelihood — and one part of wealth, since life is impermanent.
The builder of a temple of gods lifts twenty-one families and shares the wealth; with clay, wood, brick, stone and the like the fruit is in order a crore-fold.
The maker of a temple of eight bricks attains heaven. Even playing with dust, the builder of a temple of gods shares the wealth.
The fourth of the verses should increase, the Prajapatya four; one should increase by one each in the rest; up to the fourth one should discard one.
Ushnih, Anushtubh, Brihati, Pankti, Trishtubh, Jagati — these are to be known in order; the Gayatris are Brahman itself.
Three by three are the "samani," and each one is Arya; names of Rik and Yajus; one should write in sixty-four places.
With eight, sun, and sun-colors (twelve), it may be in the middle and at the end sometimes; the Brihati and Jagati — three, if Gayatri is the earlier;
the third becomes Pathya; the second the other, Kusarini. Skandhas, griva in the Krostuka; in Yaksha the Brihati also;
Brihati at the end above, Brihati in front again; sometimes four nines; in directions and corners eight-syllabled ones;
the Mahabrihati from three Jagatas, with Brihati; the Bhandila would be Pankti meter with twelve, twelve, eight, eight syllables;
the first two Veda-joined (four) and the Pankti reversed; Prastara-pankti in front; Pavada-Tara-panktika;
Akshara-pankti is five and four, two in small; Pada-pankti would be five; four, six, three —
with six and five Gayatras and six it would be Jagati; with one, Trishtubh-jyotishmati; thus Jagati is told;
in front Jyoti, in the first; in the middle Jyoti in the middle; above Jyoti from the last of one in a five;
the meter Shankumati in a six, the meter Kakudmati; Tripada-shishumadhya, that Pipilikamadhya;
Yavamadhya the reverse; Trivrit lacking one; Bhumija with one more, lacking two, after long;
Avarat with two more; doubtful from the deity and the rest. From the first foot is determination; meter and deity in order:
Agni, Sun, Moon, Jupiter, Varuna, Chandra and Vishvedevas — the notes beginning with Shadja; Shadja is the bull in order;
Gandhara, Madhyama, Panchama, Dhaivata and Nishada; colors: white, Sarangaka, tawny;
black, blue, red; Gauri among the chief Gayatri; the Kritis resembling Gauri; the meter Jyoti is dark;
Agni is Vaishya, Kashyapa; Gautama and Angirasa in order; Bhargava, Kaushika, Vashishtha — the gotras are told.
The meter here would be popular; the Vedic seers' is remembered as Trishtubh-measure only; Trishtubh, Pankti, Brihati, Anushtubh, Ushnih are told.
The sixth is "jo" preceded by nala; of the second and so on the foot in nala; in the seventh at the end the first, in the second and fifth in nala;
in the half the foot from the first; the sixth becomes a single short; a foot has three feet (gana) — Arya is remembered in five and a half;
Vipula, then Chapala, the "jau" in the middle of a heavy; the second and fourth, and in the first Chapala Mukhapurvika;
in the second Jaghanapurva; Chapalarya is declared. Of both, Mahachapala, equal to half of song and instrument;
Upagiti with the last half; Udgiti in reverse is remembered. In the half, "rakshagana" — Arya; Gitichhanda by the measure (matra);
Vaitaliya is two-voweled; in the equal feet of an odd foot "nala"; Vasus at the end and Vanagas; Gopuchchha ten;
ending in a "bhagana" is Patalika; in the rest and other as before; with the six or mixed joined, Prachya-vritti is shown;
with the fifth along with the earlier, with the third joined with a thousand: Udichya-vritti in speech and Pravartaka at once;
Charuhasini and Antika at once, unjoined.
Saptarchi and Vasus; Matrasamaka is told; Nalavama and la, or the twelfth; Navasika;
Vishvoka the fifth and eighth, "mo"; Chitra, Lavamaka, Chala; Upachitra with the following joined; Padakulaka thus;
if there is omission in Gitarya, Saumya, "la" the first; Jyoti is declared; Shikha reversed, half; Tulika is declared.
